correctness.rationale: The six integral products define a Zinbiel law. Derivation equations form an explicit 125-by-25 integer matrix with a 21-by-21 minor of determinant -4, and a 19-by-19 minor of determinant -15. Four independent central derivations exist for all fields; in characteristic 2 there are two further explicit independent derivations U,V. These prove exact Der dimensions 4 outside characteristic 2 and 6 inside. A constructive pointwise derivation for P and three independent linear constraints on any local operator prove exact LocDer dimensions 4/7, with explicit proper P. The exact determinant calculations and separate finite-field tests are reproduced by verify.py. No empirical finite enumeration is used to assert an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The recent five-dimensional Zinbiel example is a natural test case for a published local-rigidity result. Its reduction modulo two creates a mathematically sharp exception: ordinary derivations jump 4 to 6 while linear local derivations jump 4 to 7. The explicit one-dimensional quotient and exact finite-field counts pinpoint a failure of the centrality-based rigidity mechanism, rather than an arbitrary finite invariant.
